content: We need to combine subnetworks into full topology. The given subnet data have overlapping node names: Subnet1 uses A,N1,X1. Subnet2 uses N_b1,X1,X2,R1,R2,R3. Subnet3 uses X2,N1,N2,B,R1,R2,R3. Need to ensure resistor IDs unique across whole network. Also need to verify that combined topology matches all measurements. The simulation we did gave total resistance A-B = 15.859, but measurement says 41.364. So our combination is wrong; maybe connections are not as simple series linking; need to consider that subnetworks are separate but share nodes: Actually the subnetworks likely connect at nodes N1, X1, X2, N_b1 etc. The given subnet data already include connections between those nodes. So the combined topology should just merge the resistor dictionaries (renaming to avoid duplicate IDs) and concatenate connections. That we did. But the resulting A-B resistance is far off. Means the actual network may have additional connections not captured? Let's verify measurement list: many pairwise resistances. We can test our combined topology against them using validate_measurements.
